facts.text: Ta, Nb, and V were added in a 1:1:1 ratio to HfZrTi, producing HfZrTi(TaNbV)x alloys with x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9.
The HfZrTi(TaNbV)x alloys were suspension-melted under argon at 70 A for 2 min and remelted five times.
Dynamic compression and energy-release comparisons were performed in air by SHPB at a strain rate of approximately 4000 s^-1.
Increasing Ta-Nb-V transformed the alloy series from HCP through a BCC-dominant mixed-phase state to an essentially single-BCC structure at high x.
HZTX0.1 contained abundant hard, brittle omega precipitates that promoted brittle fracture and extensive fragmentation.
Ta, Nb, and V acted as beta/BCC stabilizers by lowering the BCC free energy and suppressing HCP and omega formation at sufficient concentration.
At larger x, atomic-size and modulus mismatch caused lattice distortion and solute-dislocation interactions that impeded glide and produced solid-solution strengthening.
Fragmentation exposed reactive Hf and Zr to atmospheric oxygen, causing rapid exothermic oxidation and visible sparking.
Among the compared compositions, HZTX0.1 fragmented most completely, ignited earliest, and produced the greatest combustion luminosity.
HZTX0.9 showed higher quasi-static strength and greater fracture ductility than the unalloyed HZTX0 baseline.
Under 4000 s^-1 compression in air, HZTX0.9 ignited slightly earlier and emitted more light than HZTX0.
HZTX0.9 reached a quasi-static yield strength of 1065 MPa.
